articles.title: Alex de Minaur hits career milestone in Vienna to book semi-final date with Zverev
articles.summary: World No 10 defeats Matteo Berrettini 7-6 (7-4) 6-2 in quarter-final. 27-year-old becomes ninth Australian man to reach 350 tour-level wins. Alex de Minaur has enjoyed a landmark 350th tour-level win of his career at the Vienna Open, downing an old rival to set up a semi-final date with the world…
body: Australia’s main man defeated Matteo Berrettini, the Italian he’s had plenty of trouble with down the years, for the second successive year in the quarter-final of the ATP 500 event at the Wiener Stadthalle.

Not only did his 7-6 (7-4) 6-2 triumph set “Demon” up for a third duel in just over a month with Zverev on Saturday but it boosted his bid to reach the season-ending men’s championship, the ATP Finals, which still lies in the balance.

World No 10 de Minaur found a way to draw first blood in a tight first stanza after saving a set point at 5-6, going on to take control of the tiebreak when the Italian, almost criminally, plonked a simple put-away into the net.

De Minaur crucially saved a couple of break points at the start of the next set and cashed in by himself breaking Berrettini for the first time in the next game when the Italian produced an embarrassing air-shot when faced with a straightforward smash.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso rules out January loan move for Chelsea winger Estêvão Willian
articles.summary: ‘No discussions about that … Everyone has to be ready’ Brazilian has started only twice in 11 games this season. Xabi Alonso has ruled out a January move for Estêvão Willian but has said the Chelsea youngster must adapt to his style of play before earning a regular spot in the team.
body: The debate around Estêvão’s role gathered momentum this week, with the noise growing after the 19-year-old watched as an unused substitute as Alonso’s side lost to Liverpool on penalties in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. The Brazilian became an instant hit with Chelsea fans after joining from Palmeiras last year and there are fears that the winger could look to leave after starting twice in 11 games in all competitions this season.

Yet while Estêvão is having a tougher time during his second year in English football, Alonso insisted that the Brazil international is part of his plans and will not be loaned out to get more games in January.

“No discussions about that,” Alonso said. “It’s no secret that all players want to be on the pitch. When any of them haven’t had enough minutes because of my decision, I have to take the responsibility for that. But everyone has to be ready because in any game they could be important. Este, his training and his attitude has been good.”

articles.title: Leclerc seals Mexico City practice double as Hamilton suffers technical issue
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue.
body: Leclerc produced a time of 1:17.827s to finish just over a tenth clear of McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell, with the British pair among 10 drivers who had earlier sat out the opening session to make way for rookie drivers.
Kimi Antonelli, who only needs to finish ninth in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, was a tenth down on his team-mate Russell in fourth.
Hamilton had been on course to go fastest as the session approached its midway point before suffering what appeared to be an engine issue in the final sector of his push lap.

He completed the lap but was then swiftly told by his engineer to pull over on track, ending his session early and denying him valuable information that his rivals were able to gather with their race simulations.

articles.title: Carrick tells players ‘hard truth’ in attempt to turn Manchester United’s season around
articles.summary: Head coach reflects on ‘not always rosy’ conversations. Players ‘hurting’ after eight games without a win. Michael Carrick said he has had difficult conversations with the Manchester United hierarchy and his players during their turbulent start to the season.
body: United have not won in their past eight games and start the weekend in 16th place of 20 in the league, one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position was under threat after losing last Sunday to Bournemouth but he has held on to his job for the time being and been given the chance to turn things around, starting at Chelsea on Saturday.
The head coach suggested he had spoken with the club’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, and the chief executive, Omar Berrada, this week.

“It’s pretty clear, it’s not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that’s between me and the players, whether that’s between me, Jason, Omar or the owners,” Carrick said. “It’s the truth, it’s the hard truth at times and it’s what we need to move forward. Whatever we need to move forward, we will do.”

articles.title: Araújo key factor in Liverpool’s improvement at set pieces, says Iraola
articles.summary: Reds yet to concede set-piece goal in Premier League. Szoboszlai and Muñoz could return for Arsenal game. Andoni Iraola has cited Ronald Araújo as a key factor in Liverpool’s improvement at set pieces but admitted Arsenal pose the “biggest challenge” to his team’s defensive record on Sunday.
body: Liverpool have not conceded a set-piece goal in the Premier League and have shipped only one overall, Conor Gallagher’s consolation header past Giorgi Mamardashvili in Tottenham’s Carabao Cup defeat at Anfield in September. Liverpool’s resilience stands in stark contrast to last season when Arne Slot’s side conceded 20 non-penalty set-piece goals in the Premier League. That was the joint-most in the competition alongside Crystal Palace and Iraola’s Bournemouth.

The Liverpool head coach credits his assistants, Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper, and the club analysts with this season’s set-piece figures, and says the addition of Araújo to his defence has played a major role.

“It definitely helps having a centre-back at right-back when we talk about defending set pieces,” said Iraola, who could have Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz back from injury. “It helps with the height and the physicality of the team.

“It helps us to defend better but it is true that you also lose a little bit offensively on the other side. Offensively we cannot demand of Ronald the same thing as other full-backs and what they give us, but we have to balance this with other patterns.”

articles.title: Wrexham need honest self-assessment - Parkinson
articles.summary: Phil Parkinson says he will not shy away from any criticism that comes his way following Wrexham's 1-0 Championship loss to Sheffield United at Bramall Lane.
body: Phil Parkinson says Wrexham need to conduct some "honest" self-assessments on the back of their lacklustre display against Sheffield United.
The Red Dragons were significantly below par at Bramall Lane, particularly in the first half, as Ben Brereton Diaz's 30th-minute strike earned the Blades a 1-0 victory.
After the defeat in South Yorkshire, Parkinson urged his players to be individually "self-analytical".
"However you play, it's about 11 v 11, winning your individual duels and coming out on top of the player you're against," he told BBC Radio Wales.

articles.title: Sheff Utd win first league game against Wrexham in 44 years
articles.summary: Sheffield United shook off a 44-year hoodoo by beating Wrexham 1-0 in the Championship, winning against the Welsh side in the league for the first time since October 1982.
body: It is a fixture that is turning in to one of the great EFL contests, but after their two Championship matches last term produced 11 goals, this one registered just five shots on target.
The majority were for the Blades, with Brentford loanee Romelle Donovan central to much of the good attacking play, although it was Ben Brereton Diaz who decided it.
He turned home a saved effort from Jordan Ayew for his third goal in three appearances against Wrexham, having scored in both games against them for Derby last season.
Sheffield United should have had a penalty soon after after when Dominic Hyam fouled Harrison Burrows inside the area. However, the referee waved away the claims.

articles.title: Cox sets world record to win gold at Worlds
articles.summary: Great Britain's Kadeena Cox sets a new world record as she wins C4 1km gold at the Para-cycling Track World Championships in the Netherlands.
body: The 35-year-old crossed the line in 1 minute 9.545 seconds to win her seventh world title.
Cox faced a nervous wait as Tara Neyland took to the track afterwards in pursuit of a medal, but her Australian rival could not eclipse the Briton's time.
Cox, who is a five-time Paralympic gold medallist, was draped in a British flag by her team following victory as she joyously celebrated her first world title since 2024.
In the men's tandem B 1km time-trial, Britain's James Ball defended his title as he won gold alongside new partner Aaron Pope.

articles.title: Furious Komatsu dismisses 'nonsense' reports of Bearman demanding £5m salary
articles.summary: Haas boss Ayao Komatsu has furiously dismissed reports claiming that contract extension talks with Oliver Bearman are being held up by the British driver demanding a £5m annual salary.
body: Both Bearman and Komatsu have expressed confidence in recent weeks that a deal will be done to extend the 21-year-old's current contract, which expires at the end of the 2026 season.

With Haas having already announced the signing of Bearman's fellow Ferrari junior Rafael Camara to replace Esteban Ocon next season, the lack of confirmation on his own future has led to speculation over what the issues are that are holding up the deal.
Asked on Friday at the Mexico City Grand Prix about claims that Bearman's financial demands are the main sticking point, Komatsu said: "I have no idea where that comes from.
"I've experienced this sometimes this season as well. People say there's no smoke without fire but really some people will invent a story.

articles.title: Can Robinson work Hampden magic against McInnes' Rangers?
articles.summary: Under-pressure Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson has an excellent record in Hampden semi-finals. But is Saturday's meeting with Rangers a bridge too far?
body: Ten months ago Stephen Robinson could have walked into a Paisley pub and expected a standing ovation and to drink for free all night.
In December the Northern Irishman masterminded St Mirren's second ever League Cup triumph, when his relentless and perfectly drilled side dismantled Celtic.
The pictures in the Hampden dressing room afterwards showed Robinson jumping and singing with his team after reaching the crowning moment of his tenure at the club.

It was an altogether different Robinson which appeared in front of the cameras on Wednesday night, after his Aberdeen side lost at home to Falkirk, the fourth time in six home league games they have failed to score.

articles.summary: Another Texas high school football team will forfeit a game because of injuries, leaving its season finale uncertain. Gainesville ISD announced Wednesday, Oct. 28, that its varsity football team would forfeit Friday's district matchup against Van Alstyne after injuries left the Leopards without…
body: In a letter to families and the community, Superintendent DesMontes Stewart said district and athletic leaders determined forfeiting the game was the only responsible decision.
"The health and safety of our student-athletes must remain our highest priority," Stewart wrote.
The district said it hoped injured players would recover in time for Gainesville's final regular-season game against Lake Worth.

"At this time, we are hopeful that with a week of healing that enough of the injured players will be cleared to return so that the final game of the season against Lake Worth can be played as scheduled," Stewart wrote.
